**Source:** deep-dive investigation into the swarm lifecycle commands and quality pipeline (2026-07). This is NOT part of the 10-PR minimum set (PR-A through PR-J, see #1683-#1692) — those are validated findings that survived independent adversarial re-derivation. **Everything in this issue is an UNVERIFIED CANDIDATE.** A completeness-critic pass identified 12 areas this investigation hadn't yet examined; a follow-up probe wave produced 66 candidate findings across 10 of those 12 areas, but the adversarial verification stage that would normally challenge and either confirm/revise/disprove each claim failed almost entirely (hit an account spend limit mid-run) — zero verify results were recovered. 2 of the 12 areas (external-skill-safety, LOOP-mode runaway behavior) were never even probed.

**Do not act on any claim below without independently re-deriving it from source first.** They are listed here so the investigation's coverage gap is visible and actionable, not because they're confirmed.

## Totals

66 candidate gaps across 10 lanes: 19 HIGH, 31 MEDIUM, 16 LOW (no CRITICAL claims). Two lanes never probed: **external-skill-safety**, **loop-runaway**.

## The 19 HIGH-severity candidates (lane: claim — file/evidence pointer)

**lean-turbo** (`src/turbo/lean/**`, `src/worktree/**` — opt-in parallel-lane execution):
1. Worktree-isolation success path allegedly never commits lane work before merge-back (`runner.ts:1383-1389,1116-1145`) — branch merges as "already up to date," gets deleted, work potentially stranded in an abandoned worktree while the task is marked complete.
2. A lane is allegedly marked "completed" before merge-back runs, and no gate re-checks the actual merge outcome — merge-conflicted lanes could still pass as done.
3. `integrated_diff_required` defaults true but `integratedDiffSummary` allegedly has zero writers — default lean config may deadlock at every phase boundary.
4. Lean's phase reviewer/critic — the advertised "holistic quality gate" — allegedly never sees code, only lane-count metadata; no build/test/lint runs in the lean path.
5. Failed lanes allegedly auto-commit and merge partial, unreviewed coder work into the user's HEAD with no record of it happening.

**budget-cost** (`quality_budget` gate, context-budget truncation, cost accounting):
6. `quality_budget`'s duplication metric allegedly flags any repeated line with no minimum run length — claimed to fail nearly every real source file by design (the tool's own 225-line source allegedly scores 0.188 and fails).
7. `gates.quality_budget`'s config knobs (thresholds, enabled, globs) allegedly have zero runtime consumers — can't be tuned or disabled by users who hit #6.

**failure-recovery** (circuit breakers, transient retry, orphaned delegations):
8. The coder-revision circuit breaker (default limit 5) allegedly can never trip — the counter is claimed to reset to 0 on every dispatch.
9. A coder that dies mid-task allegedly wedges the task with no recovery path short of a full session reset.

**checkpoint-rollback**:
10. `/swarm rollback` allegedly reads a checkpoint store that no production code ever writes — every user who tries the documented recovery path would get "No checkpoints found" regardless of how many checkpoints they saved.
11. Checkpoint restore is allegedly `git reset --soft`, which moves the branch pointer but restores zero file content and no `.swarm/` state — yet is claimed to be presented to the user as if it restores the tree.

**handoff-resume**:
12. `/swarm handoff`'s brief allegedly gets consumed and deleted by `system-enhancer` on the very next turn of ANY session, including the same session that just ran the command — before a genuine restart could use it.
13. Session snapshots allegedly drop `turboStrategy`/`leanTurboActive`/`epicModeActive` on restart, so a restart mid-Lean-Turbo run could downgrade to the weakest posture (QA-gate bypass survives, lean's compensating gates vanish).

**injection-defense** (untrusted external content):
14. ISSUE_INGEST issue body/comments and swarm-pr-review PR comments/reviews are allegedly fetched via raw bash `gh` and reach architect/reviewer/critic context with zero prompt-injection neutralization.
15. The sanctioned `gh_evidence` tool allegedly doesn't neutralize injection payloads either — only length-truncates.

**fallback-vs-gates** (model fallback chains):
16. Runtime model-fallback is allegedly inert — claimed to mutate only a config record that SDK agent configs never re-read, so retries could keep hitting the same failing model while telemetry claims a fallback was applied.

**full-auto-oversight**:
17. The oversight critic — described as "the sole quality gate in full-auto" — is allegedly dispatched with no diff, plan pointer, or evidence path to review.

**skill-config-upgrade**:
18. All 26 bundled skills are allegedly frozen at first-install version forever — sync is claimed to be missing-only with no version/hash check, and the plugin's own update command allegedly never re-syncs them.

**multi-session** (concurrent `.swarm/` writers):
19. `plan.json` writes are allegedly last-writer-wins — the projection write is claimed to be unlocked and built from a stale in-memory read, with a reproduced two-process race showing one session's task completion silently reverted by a concurrent session's write.

*(47 additional MEDIUM/LOW candidates exist across these same 10 lanes — omitted here for length; available on request if this issue is picked up for verification.)*

## Not probed at all

- **external-skill-safety** (can externally-influenced or LLM-generated knowledge/skill content reach agent prompts without review?)
- **loop-runaway** (LOOP-mode unattended stop conditions, error accumulation, cost runaway protection)

## Ask

If any of these turn out to be real on independent re-verification — especially #1, #2, #10, #11, and #19, which describe potential silent data loss or a documented-but-non-functional recovery path — they'd likely warrant their own dedicated PR(s) given the severity. Recommend treating this issue as a triage queue: pick a claim, re-derive it from source with fresh eyes (ideally adversarially, assuming it's wrong until proven otherwise), and split out a real issue for anything that survives.

## Priority

Unscored — pending verification.

> **Community translation** — This is an English translation of the German challenge brief so international applicants can read and tackle it. The German files in this repo (`README.md`, `dev/`, `business/`) are the authoritative source. Questions? Write to aiandbusinessgrowth@ai-at.eu. Made for fun & to learn 🌍

---

## The scenario

Energy-intensive SMEs in Austria (bakeries, cold-storage facilities, print shops) pay for electricity at day-ahead prices that vary sharply from hour to hour — at night often half as expensive as during the evening peak. Those who shift shiftable loads (dough cooling, freezer cycles, print runs) into the cheapest hours save 5–15 % on electricity costs, but mostly miss the window because no one keeps an eye on the price curve.

**Strom-Wächter** takes a daily price curve and a consumption profile and shows — within seconds — the cheapest load windows, the estimated savings, and a clear action recommendation.

---

## Choose your track

| Role | What it's about | Start here |
|---|---|---|
| **AI Developer** | Build the Strom-Wächter PoC + a short code review | 📂 [`dev/`](./dev/) |
| **AI Business Analyst & Venture Builder** | Is this a business? Business Case + Go-to-Market | 📂 [`business/`](./business/) |

> You already know from your conversation with us which track is yours — just head to the right folder. If you're unsure, drop us a quick email. (Curious about the other side? Feel free to browse. Only your folder counts for your submission.)

---

## 🛠️ AI Developer track

Welcome. This is not a trick test. It is a small, real piece of the work we do every day in the Venture Studio and n8n CoE: building something useful quickly with AI.

There is no model solution you need to match. We look at how you break down an underspecified problem, make decisions, and use AI meaningfully.

### Mission

Build a **Strom-Wächter**: a small CLI tool that takes a daily price curve and a consumption profile and produces an alert report within seconds — the cheapest load windows, the estimated savings, and a clear action recommendation ("Run at 03:00–06:00, not at 18:00").

**We provide:** a seed dataset with a 24-hour price time series (JSON + CSV, fields documented) and 3 sample consumption profiles. No domain knowledge needed: everything you need is in the dataset and this brief.

> 📂 **In the repo:** [`../data/`](../data/) — `prices.json` + `prices.csv` + sample profiles (field docs: [`../data/README.md`](../data/README.md)).
> Pattern "fetch → score → act": load a price list, score windows, output a recommendation.

### Part A: Build the PoC

- **Input:** a consumption profile (`branche`, `verschiebbare_last_kwh`, `flexibilitaet_stunden`, `region`/`bundesland`) plus a price time series (`ts`, `preis_eur_mwh`). Your tool must handle at least one of the provided sample profiles. *How* you ingest profiles (hardcoded, file, CLI argument) is up to you.
- **Output:** an alert report with the cheapest load windows for the shiftable load (length = `flexibilitaet_stunden`), each with time range and average price, plus a savings estimate (what does the load cost in the cheap window compared to a sensible baseline?) and a short action recommendation.
- **Form:** a runnable Git repo with real code, plus a README that gets us up and running in under 5 minutes. Stack is your choice (a TypeScript CLI is the obvious fit, but nothing is prescribed).

> **The interesting design decision:** What exactly is "the cheapest window"? The lowest average price across `flexibilitaet_stunden` consecutive hours? Or do you count non-consecutive hours too? How do you define the savings baseline (daily mean, daily high, evening peak)? These decisions are deliberately yours to make. We care about the reasoning, not a prescribed formula. This is exactly where we see your judgment.

> A real LLM call is allowed but not required — a deterministic or template-based recommendation is perfectly fine. No API key needed if you don't have one. (Optional stretch: live connection to the Energy-Charts API for AT prices — no key needed, but not required.)

### Part B: Code review (~15 min)

We give you a short, AI-generated TypeScript snippet. No TypeScript experience needed — the bug is language-agnostic.

**Tip:** compare what the doc-comment *promises* with what the code *does*, and trace through the code mentally with a small example.

There is one central functional bug: find it, fix it, and justify in 3–5 sentences why it is a bug. Also tell us what else you notice — missing edge cases, questionable assumptions, type modelling, missing tests. That wider critique counts just as much as the fix itself. We want to see whether you can *evaluate* AI output, not just generate it.

> The snippet is in the file [`./dev/code-review/snippet.ts`](./dev/code-review/snippet.ts).

### Developer scoring

| Dimension | Weight |
|---|---|
| Functionality (does it run, does it fulfil the core) | 20% |
| Decomposition & judgment (ambiguity resolved sensibly, good trade-offs) | 20% |
| AI collaboration / process (how you leveraged & checked AI) | 20% |
| Code quality & taste (readable, maintainable, AI "slop" spotted) | 15% |
| Communication / docs (README, decision log, walkthrough) | 15% |
| Tests (meaningful tests, no coverage theatre) | 10% |

> Part B (code review) does not feed into the table above. It is a separate signal with particularly high information value about your judgment on AI-generated code, and can tip close decisions.

---

## 📊 AI Business Analyst & Venture Builder track

Welcome. This is a real piece of Venture Studio work: assessing an idea for market readiness and making it sellable — in one week, with AI as your lever.

Our tech team is building a prototype: Strom-Wächter, an AI-powered tool that shows energy-intensive SMEs in Austria (bakeries, cold-storage facilities, print shops) when electricity is cheapest and lets them shift shiftable loads (cooling cycles, print runs, dough cooling) into the cheap hours of the day-ahead market. Savings potential: 5–15 % of electricity costs.

**Your task: Is this a business? And how do we bring it to market?**

We provide a seed dataset (24-hour price time series as JSON/CSV) and sample profiles of target businesses. The same dataset is shared with the Dev track. *The price curve illustrates the problem (volatile electricity prices); your paying customers are the SMEs that want to shift their loads.*

> ⚠️ **Important for sizing:** The data deliberately does not contain market, pricing, or conversion figures — it only shows the electricity price curve + sample profiles. You research/estimate the number of reachable customers, product price, and conversion yourself. AI and the web are there exactly for that (sources welcome). The sample profiles help you sharpen your ICP/segment, not to derive volume figures.

For this analysis, treat Strom-Wächter as a standalone commercial venture, separate from the (non-commercial, EU-funded) AI:AT context.

### Deliverables 1–4 (capped: we assess thinking, not slide design)

**1. Lean Canvas** for "Strom-Wächter" (problem-first).

**2. One-page Business Case** with:
- **Bottom-up market size.** The form matters: `‹reachable SMEs› × ‹monthly price› × ‹conversion›`. *Please no "1 % of a huge market" — a derived number beats a large one with no derivation.* Show each factor's reasoning visibly. The price itself is part of your analysis: justify it rather than assume it; relating it to the savings the tool generates for the SME is a good approach. *(Form example from a completely different industry, for structure only: 800 regional craft businesses × €29/month × 5 %.)*
- **Rough Unit Economics** (CAC, ARPU/LTV, Payback). *In short: what does a customer cost (CAC) versus what they bring in (ARPU per month, LTV over their lifetime), and after how many months is CAC recovered (Payback)? Rough, justified estimates are fine.*
- **The riskiest assumption named + one cheap test for it.**

**3. ICP + Value Proposition** for one segment (e.g. bakeries only, or cold-storage only). Tag every assumption as *validated* or *hypothesis*. Even 2–3 quick signals (brief conversations with target businesses or a landing-page smoke test) lift this deliverable from *solid* to *strong*; without them, just tag cleanly as hypothesis. (Not feasible in the time window? Clean tagging is enough — we don't expect market research.)

**4. Marketing mini-brief:** one ICP, one channel, 3 hypothetical ads (headline + body + visual idea) plus a landing-page hero (headline, subhead, CTA, 3 value bullets) plus one success metric per asset ("success = …").

**Optional stretch (this is how you stand out):** Build a working mini-automation (n8n, Make, Zapier, or a Custom-GPT) that handled part of *your own* work — e.g. market/competitive research, generating ad variants, analysing survey data. Explain the system briefly. This demonstrates "automate yourself" concretely.

> **On the 20 % "AI-Leverage" dimension:** How you use and verify AI in your work process (visible in your decision log + prompts) already counts in full. The optional automation is the path to the *top* of this dimension, not the entry ticket.

### Business scoring

| Dimension | Weight |
|---|---|
| Commercial reasoning (bottom-up, Unit Economics, consistent assumptions) | 25% |
| Customer insight / ICP (sharp segment, assumptions tagged) | 20% |
| AI leverage / "automate yourself" | 20% |
| Prioritisation / scrappiness (what you cut & why) | 15% |
| Marketing / positioning (ICP fit, channel fit, success triggers) | 10% |
| Communication / storytelling | 10% |

---

## Ground rules, submission & timeline

**Effort:** approximately 4–6 focused hours. You have a 7-calendar-day window from receipt — that window is for *flexibility*, not for grinding. Please don't over-invest: we assess thinking and judgment, not polish. *(The 4–6 hours include the walkthrough and decision log. Loom: 1 take, 3–5 min; decision log: 5–10 bullet lines.)*

**Use any AI, any library, search freely.** This is expected, not just allowed. Cursor, Claude, Copilot, coding agents — go for it.

**A rough core with clear thinking beats a polished but shallow result.** More hours do not mean more points; we assess the core outcome, not time invested.

**Equal opportunity:** AI Factory Austria is committed to equal opportunity. Whether you come from university, a bootcamp, or are self-taught — what counts is *how* you think and work with AI. If you need support or adjustments in the process, let us know.

### What to submit

1. **Repo link** (GitHub/GitLab) with code + README *(Dev track)* or documents *(Business track)*.
2. **Walkthrough (1 take, 3–5 min, max 5):** a Loom or screen recording. Show your result and explain *how* you built/researched it — especially the AI steps. *(No video possible or preferred? A concise written walkthrough counts equally — just let us know.)*
3. **Short decision log + key AI prompts:** 5–10 lines of decisions/trade-offs plus the AI prompts that made a difference. Show us *how you work with AI* — that is exactly the skill we are hiring for.
4. **Self-report:** how many hours did you invest? (Honest answer — no penalty points.)

**Submission:** by email to aiandbusinessgrowth@ai-at.eu. Your specific deadline and any upload link are in the accompanying email.

**Response time:** we get back to you within ~10 working days with a slot for the live debrief or a brief update.

**The live debrief (30–45 min):** you walk us through your result, we set *one new requirement live* and watch how you extend your own work. The new requirement is deliberately small — it's about thinking out loud, not producing a perfect result in 10 minutes. You may use your usual AI tools, exactly as when building. Afterwards we show you our own solution and talk honestly about it.

**Fair & transparent:** this challenge is unpaid. In return, after the debrief we show you our own reference solution — with real decisions, prompts, and trade-offs. That is our "learn" promise in action. And: structured, honest feedback for everyone, whatever the outcome. No ghosting. Ever.

---

## Data & privacy

The seed dataset is synthetic/simplified (as of 2026-06) and does not represent an official AI:AT position. No domain knowledge is required — the price curve and profiles are self-explanatory. Field documentation is in [`./data/README.md`](./data/README.md) (kept in German for now).

Your submitted documents (repo link, Loom link, files, prompts) will be used solely for the hiring decision, will not be shared with uninvolved third parties, and will be deleted no later than **six months** after the conclusion of the selection process (or earlier on your request), in accordance with GDPR. The legal basis is the initiation of a possible employment relationship (Art. 6 GDPR); you may request access or deletion at any time. Anything you create remains yours — we use it only for assessment, never in production. Questions: aiandbusinessgrowth@ai-at.eu.

---

🇦🇹 *If anything is unclear, the German original in this repo is authoritative.*

# Work package: π₁ of a punctured sphere is free (SVK-lite)

**Self-contained — no prior context needed.** This issue is written so an external collaborator (human or agent) can start cold. Repo: [`mrdouglasny/jacobian-challenge`](https://github.com/mrdouglasny/jacobian-challenge) — a Lean 4 + Mathlib formalization of Jacobians of compact Riemann surfaces (Buzzard's Jacobian challenge). Toolchain and Mathlib pin: see `lean-toolchain` / `lake-manifest.json` (Mathlib `c5ea003`).

## Why this matters (the one paragraph)

The project's deepest remaining axiom is `AX_PeriodCycleBasis` (`Jacobians/Axioms/PeriodCycleBasis.lean:237`): every compact connected Riemann surface admits `2g` piecewise-real-analytic loops whose classes form a ℤ-basis of `H₁` and satisfy Riemann's bilinear relations arc-level. The approved general-X discharge route (`docs/planning/CYCLEBASIS_ALTERNATIVES.md`, direction 2b) avoids surface classification entirely: a Riemann–Roch-supplied meromorphic function exhibits `X` as a finite branched cover of ℙ¹, and the classical *slit-sheet* construction then produces the cycle basis from covering theory over the punctured sphere. Every other ingredient of that route either exists (covering machinery, Nielsen–Schreier, the port's boundary-word R1/R2 engine) or is incremental bookkeeping. The single piece of genuinely new topology — **the only research-grade obstacle left on the challenge-critical path** — is: *the fundamental group of a punctured sphere/plane is free, on explicit loops around the punctures*. That is this work package.

## Target statements (the contract)

Stated against Mathlib's `FundamentalGroup` (`Mathlib.AlgebraicTopology.FundamentalGroupoid.FundamentalGroup`). Exact Lean spelling is the implementer's choice **up to mathematical content**; the content below is frozen (see "Interface freeze" at the end).

**T1 (plane minus finite set — the main theorem).** For a finite set `S : Finset ℂ` and a basepoint `x₀ : ↥((↑S : Set ℂ)ᶜ)`:

```lean
-- (suggested shape; any equivalent packaging of the same content is fine)
theorem fundamentalGroup_compl_finite_free
    (S : Finset ℂ) (x₀ : ((↑S : Set ℂ)ᶜ : Set ℂ)) :
    ∃ (γ : S → Path x₀ x₀)
      (e : FundamentalGroup ((↑S : Set ℂ)ᶜ : Set ℂ) x₀ ≃* FreeGroup S),
      ∀ s : S, e.symm (FreeGroup.of s) = FundamentalGroup.fromPath ⟦γ s⟧
      -- plus: each γ s winds once (positively) around the puncture s
      -- and around no other puncture — pin this via an explicit
      -- construction (small circle around s conjugated by a spoke
      -- from x₀), not just abstractly.
```

i.e. `π₁(ℂ ∖ S)` is **free on `|S|` generators, and the free generators are explicit loops around the punctures**. The "generators = puncture loops" clause is load-bearing: the downstream slit-sheet construction lifts *these specific loops* through a branched covering, so abstract freeness alone (`IsFreeGroup` with no named generators) does **not** satisfy the contract.

**T2 (sphere corollary).** For `n + 1` distinct points on the Riemann sphere (equivalently: remove one point, identify the rest with `ℂ` via the standard chart), `π₁(sphere ∖ {p₀, …, pₙ})` is free on `n` generators — the loops around `p₁, …, pₙ`, with the relation "product of all `n+1` puncture loops = 1" absorbing the loop around `p₀`. Any sphere model already in Mathlib or in this repo is acceptable (`Metric.sphere (0 : EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin 3)) 1`, `RiemannSphere`, or `ℂ ∪ {∞}` via a chart + T1); state which one and how it converts.

**Consumer form.** The slit-sheet construction will consume T1/T2 as: the restriction of a degree-`d` branched cover `f : X → ℙ¹` away from the branch locus is a covering map; `π₁(X ∖ f⁻¹(branch points))` embeds as an index-`d` subgroup of the free group of T2; Nielsen–Schreier (in Mathlib) makes it free; rank bookkeeping is Riemann–Hurwitz. So the deliverable must compose with `IsCoveringMap` monodromy/lifting — keep the statement basepointed and `Path`-level, not just abstract-group-level.

## What exists (verified at Mathlib pin `c5ea003`)

In Mathlib:
- `FundamentalGroup X x` + basepoint transport `FundamentalGroup.fundamentalGroupMulEquivOfPath` — `Mathlib.AlgebraicTopology.FundamentalGroupoid.FundamentalGroup`.
- `FundamentalGroupoid` — `Mathlib.AlgebraicTopology.FundamentalGroupoid.Basic`; `SimplyConnectedSpace`, `simply_connected_iff_loops_nullhomotopic` — `....SimplyConnected`.
- **Nielsen–Schreier**: `subgroupIsFreeOfIsFree` — `Mathlib.GroupTheory.FreeGroup.NielsenSchreier` (via `IsFreeGroupoid`); `IsFreeGroup` — `Mathlib.GroupTheory.FreeGroup.IsFreeGroup`.
- **Covering maps**: `IsCoveringMap` — `Mathlib.Topology.Covering.Basic`; path lifting + monodromy: `IsCoveringMap.liftPath`, `IsCoveringMap.monodromyFunctor`, and the Hatcher-1.33 lifting criterion `IsCoveringMap.existsUnique_continuousMap_lifts_of_range_le` — `Mathlib.Topology.Homotopy.Lifting`.
- `AddCircle.isCoveringMap_coe` (`ℝ → AddCircle p` is a covering map) — `Mathlib.Topology.Covering.AddCircle`.
- `Path.subpath`, `Path.concat`, `Path.Homotopic.concat_subpath` — `Mathlib.Topology.Subpath`.

**Absent from Mathlib at pin** (confirmed by search): `π₁(S¹) ≃ ℤ` (no computation of any circle's fundamental group), any *topological* Seifert–van Kampen (only the categorical `Mathlib.CategoryTheory.Limits.VanKampen`), `π₁` of a punctured plane, cellular homology, surface classification.

In this repo (Apache 2.0, vendored, compiles in our build):
- **Kirov's two-open SVK skeleton**: `vendor/kirov-dolbeault-port/KirovDolbeault/VanKampen.lean` — a fully *proven* two-open van Kampen for the **simply-connected conclusion** (`twoOpenVanKampen_holds`), built from Lebesgue subdivision of a loop (`exists_lebesgue_subdivision`), spokes through the overlap, per-arc nullhomotopy, and a clean fundamental-groupoid telescoping core (`telescope`, `cancel_conj`, `concat_nullhomotopic`). It is *not* a π₁-presentation SVK, but the subdivision/spokes/telescoping method is exactly what the full statement needs — the hard quotient-algebra plumbing is already done and reusable.

## Suggested milestones

1. **Base case: `π₁(ℂ ∖ {p}) ≃* Multiplicative ℤ`** (equivalently free on one generator), generator = the loop once around `p`. Route: deformation-retract `ℂ ∖ {p}` onto a circle, compute the circle's π₁ from the `ℝ → AddCircle` covering (`AddCircle.isCoveringMap_coe`) + monodromy from `Mathlib.Topology.Homotopy.Lifting`. This is new to Mathlib and independently valuable.
2. **Two-open SVK with free-product conclusion.** Either (a) extend Kirov's telescoping engine: track which open each Lebesgue arc lies in, producing a word in the free product, and prove the two-open SVK for π₁ (or the fundamental groupoid pushout, implementer's choice); or (b) a direct deformation-retract/induction route avoiding general SVK, if you see one that stays within Mathlib's current toolkit. (a) is recommended — the method is de-risked.
3. **Induction on `|S|`** to T1, keeping the generators-are-puncture-loops pin explicit at every step (spoke-conjugated small circles).
4. **T2 sphere corollary** via a chart.

## Deliverable form

- **Either** PR(s) to this repo under a new `Jacobians/Topology/` module (does not exist yet — create it), **or** a standalone Lake project at the same toolchain + Mathlib pin that we then vendor. Both accepted; incremental PRs per milestone are encouraged.
- **Standard-3 axioms only**: every theorem must `#print axioms` to at most `propext`, `Classical.choice`, `Quot.sound`. No new `axiom` declarations, no `sorry` in merged PRs.
- Pre-push gate per `CLAUDE.md`: validate any commit touching ≥20 LOC of Lean with `lake env lean <file.lean>` before pushing (the LSP diagnostics tool is unreliable as a push gate).
- Mathlib-ready style preferred (this is upstreamable material — `π₁(S¹) ≃ ℤ` and topological SVK are long-standing Mathlib gaps).

## Interface freeze

The consuming construction (the slit-sheet cycle basis, direction 2b of `docs/planning/CYCLEBASIS_ALTERNATIVES.md`) is expected to start in **a few weeks**. The target statements above are the contract it will be written against. If you want to change the statement shape (e.g. groupoid-level instead of based, different generator packaging), **propose it in this issue first** — do not let a PR be the first appearance of an interface change.

Related: #16 (the parent axiom-discharge tracker; see its 2026-06-10 comments for the full route audit), `docs/planning/CYCLEBASIS_ALTERNATIVES.md` §2b, §3.

---
Coordination: comment here to claim; the axiom interface is frozen — propose interface changes in this thread before PRs.

# Proposal: Four-Tier Library Architecture & Version Governance for Lean 4

## Summary

This proposal aims to solve the pervasive version fragmentation problem in the Lean 4 ecosystem by establishing a clear hierarchical system and improved version management.

## Motivation

The Lean 4 ecosystem currently faces significant challenges:

1. **Version Churn**: Lean 4 adopts a monthly minor release cadence with frequent breaking changes
2. **Compatibility Issues**: Code written for v4.20 often fails to compile on v4.21 without modification
3. **Mathlib & Toolchain Coupling**: Mathlib is tightly bound to specific Lean versions, creating cascading compatibility issues
4. **Duplicated Dependencies**: Every project downloads complete toolchains and dependencies independently
5. **Version Number Confusion**: `v4.9.0` to `v4.10.0` appears like a major version jump when it's actually just the 10th minor release

These issues create significant friction for users, library authors, and the community at large.

## Proposed Solution

### 1. Four-Tier Library Architecture

We propose establishing a hierarchical stability system:

```
Level 1: Standard Syntax (2-year cycle)
  └─ Core language syntax, inductive types, basic tactics
  └─ No breaking changes guaranteed
  └─ Example: `intro`, `exact`, `apply`, `rfl`

Level 2: Standard Library (1-year cycle)
  └─ Stable API subset of core data structures
  └─ `List`, `Array`, `Option`, standard typeclasses
  └─ `BEq`, `Ord`, `Hashable`, `Functor`, `Monad`
  └─ Core `simp` framework

Level 3: Feature Libraries (quarterly cycle)
  └─ New features, performance optimizations
  └─ `Std.Data.HashMap`, `Lean.Meta.Omega`
  └─ Can migrate to Level 2 after validation

Level 4: Incubating Libraries (no fixed cycle)
  └─ Experimental features, third-party contributions
  └─ No stability guarantees
  └─ Warnings on import
```

### 2. Improved Version Numbering

Current: `vMAJOR.MINOR.PATCH`
Proposed: `vMAJOR.XX.PATCH-LEVEL`

**Advantages**:
- Two-digit minor versions avoid confusion (`v4.09.0` → `v4.10.0` appears natural)
- `LEVEL` suffix indicates stability level:
  - `-1`: Standard Syntax level compatibility
  - `-2`: Standard Library level compatibility
  - `-3`: Feature Libraries level compatibility
  - `-4`: Incubating Libraries level compatibility

**Examples**:
- `v5.00.0-1`: Major Standard Syntax update
- `v4.30.0-2`: Standard Library annual update
- `v4.29.1-3`: Feature Libraries quarterly update

### 3. Shared Dependency Library Specification

Establish a global cache system:

```
~/.lean4/shared/
├── toolchains/
│   ├── lean4-v4.29.0/
│   └── lean4-v4.30.0/
├── stdlibs/
│   ├── level1/v4.x/
│   ├── level2/v4.29/
│   └── level3/v4.29/
└── community/
    ├── mathlib/stable-v4.29/
    └── other_libs/
```

**New Lake Configuration**:
```toml
[shared_dependencies]
enabled = true
cache_dir = "~/.lean4/shared"
```

**New Lake Commands**:
```bash
lake shared list                # List all shared libraries
lake shared update mathlib      # Update shared library
lake shared clean               # Clean up expired shared libraries
lake shared install lean4-v4.30 # Install new toolchain to shared directory
```

### 4. Stability Annotation System

Add standardized attributes:

```lean
-- Core attributes
@[stable_since "v4.0"]
def List.map (f : α → β) (l : List α) : List β := ...

@[deprecated_since "v4.25" "use List.Stable.find instead"]
def List.find (p : α → Bool) (l : List α) : Option α := ...

@[experimental_since "v4.30"]
def List.newFeature : ... := ...

@[moved_to "Lean.Stable.Data.List.find"]
def List.oldFind : ... := ...

@[incubating_warning "This API may change without notice"]
def Lean.Incubating.experimental : ... := ...
```

## Compatibility Matrix

| Your Code Uses | Compatible Lean Versions |
|--------------|-----------------------|
| Standard Syntax only (Level 1) | v4.x, v5.x (2 years) |
| Standard Library (Level 2) | v4.20-v4.30 (1 year) |
| Feature Libraries (Level 3) | v4.28-v4.30 (1 quarter) |
| Incubating Libraries (Level 4) | Current version only |

## Migration Path

### Short-Term (3 months)
1. Establish stability annotation system
2. Create `Lean.Stable` namespace with curated stable APIs
3. Document stability levels of existing APIs

### Medium-Term (6-12 months)
1. Officially launch four-tier architecture
2. Align mathlib with similar structure (`Mathlib.Stable.*`, `Mathlib.Feature.*`)
3. Implement version management tools:
   - `lake check-compat`: Check compatibility
   - `lake migrate`: Auto-migrate to new APIs

### Long-Term (2 years)
1. First LTS version (v5.0.0) with 5-year support
2. Complete ecosystem adoption of four-tier architecture

## Impact

This proposal would:
- ✅ Reduce maintenance burden for library authors
- ✅ Make user code more portable across versions
- ✅ Save disk space with shared dependencies
- ✅ Provide clear stability expectations
- ✅ Still allow rapid iteration in feature/incubating tiers

## References

- Based on analysis of Lean 4 version history (v4.0.0 through v4.29.1)
- Inspired by other languages with strong stability guarantees (Rust editions, Python stdlib)

## The scenario

EU companies with supply chains have been required since the **CSDDD** (Corporate Sustainability Due Diligence Directive) to screen their suppliers for geopolitical, sanctions, and ESG risks. Done manually, this means hours of research per supplier across heterogeneous sources: governance indices, sanctions lists, trade statistics.

**Lieferketten-Check** takes a supplier list and generates — within seconds — an explainable risk score with a traffic-light rating for each supplier. An automated first-pass that shows which suppliers are green (non-critical) and which need a deeper review (amber/red).

---

## Choose your track

| Role | What it's about | Start here |
|---|---|---|
| **AI Developer** | Build the Lieferketten-Check agent + a short code review | 📂 [`dev/`](./dev/) |
| **AI Business Analyst & Venture Builder** | Is this a business? Business Case + Go-to-Market | 📂 [`business/`](./business/) |

---

## 🛠️ AI Developer track

This is not a trick test. It is a real piece of the work we do every day in the Venture Studio and n8n CoE: building something useful quickly with AI.

There is no model solution you need to match. We look at how you break down an underspecified problem, make decisions, and use AI meaningfully.

### Mission

EU companies with supply chains must screen their suppliers for geopolitical, sanctions, and ESG risks under the CSDDD. Done manually, that's hours of research per supplier across heterogeneous sources: governance indices, sanctions lists, trade statistics.

Build a **Lieferketten-Check** agent: a TS/Node tool that reads a supplier list and generates an explainable risk score with a traffic-light rating for each supplier. An automated CSDDD first-pass that shows which suppliers are green (non-critical) and which need a deeper review (amber/red).

We provide a seed dataset with 28 synthetic suppliers from 12 countries (JSON), each with name, country, commodity group, trade volume, and three already-normalised risk dimensions (Geopolitics/Governance, Sanctions Exposure, Trade Exposure). No domain knowledge needed — everything is in the dataset and this brief.

> 📂 **In the repo:** [`../data/`](../data/) — `suppliers.json`, `suppliers.csv`, and example profiles (field docs: [`../data/README.md`](../data/README.md)).
> Pattern "fetch → enrich → aggregate → report": load the supplier list, aggregate the dimensions, output the report.

### Part A: Build the agent (required)

- **Input:** `suppliers.json` — per supplier: `lieferant_id`, `name`, `land_iso2`, `land_name`, `branche`, `hs_code`, `ware`, `handelsvolumen_eur_jahr`, and three risk dimensions (all 0–100, high = more risk).
- **Output:** for each supplier an explainable risk report:
  - **Risk score** 0–100 (aggregated from the three dimensions)
  - **Traffic light:** green / amber / red
  - **Driver justification:** which dimensions are driving the score (at least 1–2 sentences)
  - **Action recommendation** (first-pass: e.g. "non-critical", "deeper review recommended", "immediate escalation")
  - Plus a **portfolio overview:** all suppliers sorted by risk (highest first), with traffic-light distribution.
- **Form:** a runnable Git repo with real code, plus a README that gets us up and running in under 5 minutes, without an API key and running deterministically on the seed. Stack is your choice (TypeScript/tsx is the obvious fit, but nothing is prescribed).

> **The interesting design decision:** The three risk dimensions have different levels of relevance. How do you weight them into a score, and how do you justify that? (Geopolitics more than Trade? Sanctions as a hard blocker?) There is no prescribed formula — and that is exactly the signal. Document your weighting as an explicit assumption in the README or a code comment. Also: what do you do when a dimension is missing or 0? Ignore it, apply a default value, or mark the score as "insufficient data"?

> A real LLM call is allowed — e.g. for the justification texts or action recommendations — but not required. Rule-based texts are perfectly fine, and no API key is needed. (Optional stretch: live connection to World Bank WGI / UN Comtrade / EU sanctions list via a `--live` flag, with a deterministic fallback to the seed. No key needed on the public paths.)

### Part B: Code review (~15 min)

We give you a short, AI-generated code snippet (TypeScript — no TypeScript experience needed, the bug is language-agnostic). Tip: compare what the doc-comment *promises* with what the code *does*, and trace through the code mentally with a high-risk example.

There is one central functional bug. Find it, fix it, and justify in 3–5 sentences why it is a bug. Also tell us what else you notice: missing edge cases, questionable assumptions, missing normalisation handling, missing tests. That wider critique counts just as much as the fix itself. We want to see whether you can *evaluate* AI output, not just generate it.

> The snippet is in [`./dev/code-review/snippet.ts`](./dev/code-review/snippet.ts).

### Developer scoring

| Dimension | Weight |
|---|---|
| Functionality (does it run, does it fulfil the core) | 20% |
| Decomposition & judgment (aggregation justified, gaps handled sensibly, good trade-offs) | 20% |
| AI collaboration / process (how you leveraged & checked AI) | 20% |
| Code quality & taste (readable, maintainable, AI "slop" spotted) | 15% |
| Communication / docs (README, decision log, walkthrough) | 15% |
| Tests (meaningful tests, no coverage theatre) | 10% |

> Part B (code review) does not feed into the table above. It is a separate signal with particularly high information value about your judgment on AI-generated code, and can tip close decisions.

---

## 📊 AI Business Analyst & Venture Builder track

Welcome. This is a real piece of Venture Studio work: assessing an idea for market readiness and making it sellable — in one week, with AI as your lever.

Our tech team is building a prototype: Lieferketten-Check, an AI agent that reads a supplier list and generates an explainable Geopolitics/Sanctions/ESG risk score for each supplier. The backdrop: the **CSDDD** obliges a growing number of EU companies to systematically screen their supply chains, and doing it manually means hours of research per supplier from heterogeneous sources.

**Your task: Is this a business? And how do we bring it to market?**

We provide a seed dataset (synthetic supplier list as JSON, 28 suppliers from 12 countries with industries, commodity groups, and risk dimensions). The same dataset is shared with the Dev track. *The dataset illustrates the problem (heterogeneous risk exposures across the supply chain); your paying customers are the companies that need to fulfil CSDDD due diligence obligations.*

> ⚠️ **Important for sizing:** The data deliberately contains no market, pricing, or conversion figures — it only shows synthetic supplier profiles. The number of reachable customers (e.g. how many Austrian/European companies above what size fall under CSDDD), the product price, and conversion are yours to research/estimate. AI and the web are there exactly for that (sources welcome). The supplier profiles help you sharpen your ICP/segment (e.g. which industries have the highest CSDDD urgency), not to derive volume figures.

For this analysis, treat Lieferketten-Check as a standalone commercial venture, separate from the (non-commercial, EU-funded) AI:AT context.

### Deliverables (capped — we assess thinking, not slide design)

**1. Lean Canvas** for "Lieferketten-Check" (problem-first).

**2. One-page Business Case** with:
- **Bottom-up market size.** The form matters: `‹reachable companies with CSDDD obligation› × ‹monthly price› × ‹conversion›`. *Please no "1 % of a huge market" — a derived number beats a large one with no derivation.* Show each factor's reasoning visibly. The price itself is part of your analysis: justify it rather than assume it — relating it to the effort the tool saves the company is a good approach. *(Form example from a completely different industry, for structure only: 800 regional craft businesses × €29/month × 5 %.)*
- **Rough Unit Economics** (CAC, ARPU/LTV, Payback). *In short: what does a customer cost (CAC) versus what they bring in (ARPU per month, LTV over their lifetime), and after how many months is CAC recovered (Payback)? Rough, justified estimates are fine.*
- **The riskiest assumption named + one cheap test for it.**

**3. ICP + Value Proposition** for one segment (e.g. Austrian mid-market manufacturers only, or textile/fashion supply chains only). Tag every assumption as *validated* or *hypothesis*. Even 2–3 quick signals (brief conversations with Procurement/Compliance stakeholders or a landing-page smoke test) lift this deliverable from *solid* to *strong*; without them, just tag cleanly as hypothesis. (Not feasible in the time window? Clean tagging is enough — we don't expect market research.)

**4. Marketing mini-brief:** one ICP, one channel, **3 hypothetical ads** (headline + body + visual idea), a **landing-page hero** (headline, subhead, CTA, 3 value bullets), and **one success metric per asset** ("success = …").

**Optional stretch (this is how you stand out):** Build a working mini-automation (n8n, Make, Zapier, or a Custom-GPT) that handled part of *your own* work — e.g. market/competitive research on CSDDD tools, generating ad variants, analysing industry sources. Explain the system briefly. This demonstrates "automate yourself" concretely.

> **On the 20% "AI-Leverage" dimension:** How you use and verify AI in your work process (visible in your decision log + prompts) already counts in full. The optional automation is the path to the *top* of this dimension, not the entry ticket.

### Business scoring

| Dimension | Weight |
|---|---|
| Commercial reasoning (bottom-up, Unit Economics, consistent assumptions) | 25% |
| Customer insight / ICP (sharp segment, assumptions tagged) | 20% |
| AI leverage / "automate yourself" | 20% |
| Prioritisation / scrappiness (what you cut & why) | 15% |
| Marketing / positioning (ICP fit, channel fit, success triggers) | 10% |
| Communication / storytelling | 10% |

---

## Ground rules, submission & timeline

**Effort:** approximately 4–6 focused hours. You have a 7-calendar-day window from receipt — that window is for *flexibility*, not for grinding. Please don't over-invest: we assess thinking and judgment, not polish. *(The hours include the walkthrough and decision log. Loom: 1 take, 3–5 min; decision log: 5–10 bullet lines.)*

**Use any AI, any library, search freely.** This is expected, not just allowed. Cursor, Claude, Copilot, coding agents — go for it.

**A rough core with clear thinking beats a polished but shallow result.** More hours do not mean more points; we assess the core outcome, not time invested.

**Equal opportunity:** AI Factory Austria is committed to equal opportunity. Whether you come from university, a bootcamp, or are self-taught — what counts is *how* you think and work with AI. If you need support or adjustments in the process, let us know.

### What to submit

1. **Repo link** (GitHub/GitLab) with code + README.
2. **Walkthrough (1 take, 3–5 min, max 5):** a Loom or screen recording. Show your result and explain *how* you built it — especially the AI steps. *(No video possible or preferred? A concise written walkthrough counts equally — just let us know.)*
3. **Short decision log + key AI prompts:** 5–10 lines of decisions/trade-offs plus the AI prompts that made a difference. Show us *how you work with AI* — that is exactly the skill we are hiring for.
4. **Self-report:** how many hours did you invest? (Honest answer — no penalty points.)

**Submission:** by email to aiandbusinessgrowth@ai-at.eu. Your specific deadline and any upload link are in the accompanying email.

**Response time:** we get back to you within ~10 working days with a slot for the live debrief or a brief update.

**The live debrief (30–45 min):** you walk us through your result, we set one new requirement live and watch how you extend your own work. Afterwards we show you our own solution and talk honestly about it.

**Fair & transparent:** this challenge is unpaid. In return, after the debrief we show you our own reference solution — with real decisions, prompts, and trade-offs. Structured, honest feedback for everyone, whatever the outcome. No ghosting. Ever.

## The scenario

A location decision is a **€500K+ commitment** for an expanding Austrian business (retail chain, retailer, logistics operator, restaurant chain) — and today it is often made on gut instinct or through expensive consultants. **Standort-Agent** is an AI system that takes a business profile and shows — within seconds — which Austrian municipalities/districts are the best fit and why, evaluated across multiple signals (demographics, POI/surroundings density, rental costs, public-transport connectivity).

## 🛠️ AI Developer track

Welcome. This is not a trick test. It is a small, real piece of the work we do every day in the Venture Studio and n8n CoE: building something genuinely useful with AI, fast. This time it's a bit more ambitious: a multi-agent system.

There is no model solution you need to match. We look at how you break down an underspecified problem into sub-tasks, design an architecture, make decisions, and use AI as a lever — and how you scrutinise it.

### Mission

A location decision is a **€500K+ commitment** for an expanding Austrian business (retail chain, retailer, logistics operator). Build a "Standort-Agent": a system that takes a business profile (e.g. retail, 200 m², target audience young professionals, rental budget) and delivers a justified location ranking across Austrian municipalities — with a transparent rationale per municipality per signal, plus an interactive HTML report.

The crux: location assessment is multi-dimensional. Demographics, POI/surroundings density, rental costs, and public-transport connectivity pull in different directions. That is exactly what makes it a compelling multi-agent problem: one specialised sub-agent per signal, and an orchestrator that aggregates and weights.

We provide a seed dataset of 20 municipalities (`municipalities.json` + `municipalities.csv`, fields documented) and 2–3 sample profiles. No domain knowledge needed: everything you need is in the dataset.

> 📂 In the repo: [`../data/`](../data/) with `municipalities.json`, `municipalities.csv`, and sample profiles under [`../data/examples/`](../data/examples/) (field docs: [`../data/README.md`](../data/README.md)).

### Part A: Build the PoC

- **Input:** a business profile (`branche`, `flaeche_m2`, `zielgruppe`, `budget_miete_eur`, `region_praeferenz`). Your tool must handle at least one of the provided sample profiles. How you ingest profiles (file, CLI argument, etc.) is up to you.
- **Processing:** four signals — demographics (age structure ↔ target audience), POI/surroundings (POI density ↔ sector), rent (rental index ↔ budget), and public transport (connectivity ↔ target audience). Each signal is converted to a partial score; the orchestrator aggregates them into a weighted overall ranking.
- **Output:** a justified ranking of the most suitable municipalities — e.g. the top 3–5 (the number is your call; justify it briefly), each with "fits because… / doesn't fit because…" per signal, plus an interactive HTML report with a ranking table and rationales.
- **Form:** a runnable Git repo with real code and a README that gets us up and running in under 5 minutes. Stack: Python (≥ 3.11). Which libraries, whether CLI or more, is entirely up to you.

> **The interesting architecture decision:** We deliberately say "multi-agent". An orchestrator coordinating specialised sub-agents is the expected shape and the natural decomposition of this problem. *How* you implement it (custom classes/functions, an agent framework, one LLM per sub-agent, or pure heuristics) is precisely where we see your judgment. A well-argued non-multi-agent approach is not automatically wrong — but then we expect the reasoning for why a different decomposition is better here.

> **The other judgment call:** The signals come in different units and scales (e.g. population shares 0–1, density scores 0–10, rental index in €/m²), and some are a benefit (higher = better) while others are a cost/risk factor (higher = worse). How you bring both onto a comparable basis before weighted aggregation is your design decision. We look at the reasoning, not a prescribed formula.

> Real LLM calls (e.g. for the generated rationales) are allowed but not required: a deterministic or template-based rationale is perfectly fine. No API key needed if you don't have one — the base run must work without a key.

### Part B: Code review (~15 min)

We give you a short, AI-generated Python snippet. Tip: compare what the doc-comment *promises* with what the code *does*, and keep in mind the note about scales and direction above. There is one central functional bug: find it, fix it, and justify in 3–5 sentences why it is a bug. Also tell us what else you notice — missing edge cases, questionable assumptions, missing validation. That wider critique counts just as much as the fix itself. We want to see whether you can *evaluate* AI output, not just generate it.

> The snippet is in the file [`./dev/code-review/snippet.py`](./dev/code-review/snippet.py).

|---|---|
| Functionality (does it run, does it fulfil the core: orchestrator + sub-agents → ranking + report) | 20% |
| Decomposition & judgment (sensible multi-agent split, good trade-offs, ambiguity resolved) | 20% |
| AI collaboration / process (how you leveraged & checked AI) | 20% |
| Code quality & taste (readable, maintainable, consistent sub-agent interface, AI "slop" spotted) | 15% |
| Communication / docs (README, decision log, walkthrough) | 15% |
| Tests (meaningful tests, no coverage theatre) | 10% |

Also tell us what else you notice — missing edge cases, questionable assumptions, missing validation. That wider critique counts just as much as the fix itself. We want to see whether you can *evaluate* AI output, not just generate it.

> The snippet is in the file [`./dev/code-review/snippet.py`](./dev/code-review/snippet.py). Do not reproduce the code in your submission — a clear written explanation is sufficient.

### Developer scoring

| Dimension | Weight |
|---|---|
| Functionality (does it run, does it fulfil the core) | 20% |
| Decomposition & judgment (ambiguity resolved sensibly, good trade-offs) | 20% |
| AI collaboration / process (how you leveraged & checked AI) | 20% |
| Code quality & taste (readable, maintainable, AI "slop" spotted) | 15% |
| Communication / docs (README, decision log, walkthrough) | 15% |
| Tests (meaningful tests, no coverage theatre) | 10% |

> Part B (code review) does not feed into the table above. It is a separate signal with particularly high information value about your judgment on AI-generated code, and can tip close decisions.

---

## 📊 AI Business Analyst & Venture Builder track

Welcome. This is a real piece of Venture Studio work: assessing an idea for market readiness and making it sellable — in one week, with AI as your lever.

Our tech team is building a prototype: ESG-Radar, an AI assistant that reads in a company's sustainability disclosures, checks them against sector benchmarks, scores gaps and compliance risks, and outputs a CSRD readiness report with prioritised actions in minutes. The market pressure is set: the **CSRD** compels tens of thousands of EU companies to disclose their sustainability under the ESRS standard, and many do not know where they stand. Your task: Is this a business? And how do we bring it to market?

We provide a seed dataset as orientation (sample companies with ESG KPIs as JSON/CSV plus sector benchmarks; the CSV opens conveniently in Excel/Sheets). *It shows you the type of data ESG-Radar works with. Your paying customers are the companies that need to become CSRD-ready.*

> ⚠️ **Important for sizing:** The data deliberately contains no market, pricing, or conversion figures (it shows only sample KPIs). You research or estimate the number of reachable customers, the price, and conversion yourself — AI and the web are there exactly for that (sources welcome). The sample companies help you sharpen your ICP/segment, not to derive volume figures.

For this analysis, treat ESG-Radar as a standalone commercial venture, separate from the (non-commercial, EU-funded) AI:AT context.

### Deliverables (capped: we assess thinking, not slide design)

1. **Lean Canvas** for "ESG-Radar" (problem-first).
2. **One-page Business Case** with:
   - **Bottom-up market size.** The form matters: `‹reachable customers› × ‹price› × ‹conversion›`. *Please no "1 % of 50,000 CSRD companies" — a derived number beats a large one with no derivation.* Show each factor's reasoning visibly. The price itself is part of your analysis (justify it; don't just assume it). *(Form example from a completely different industry, for structure only: 800 regional craft businesses × €29/month × 5 %.)*
   - **Rough Unit Economics** (CAC, ARPU/LTV, Payback). *In short: what does a customer cost (CAC) vs. what they bring in (ARPU per month, LTV over their lifetime), and after how many months is CAC recovered (Payback)? Rough, justified estimates are fine.*
   - **The riskiest assumption named + one cheap test for it.**
3. **ICP + Value Proposition** for **one** segment. Tag every assumption as *validated* or *hypothesis*. Even 2–3 quick signals (brief conversations with target customers or a landing-page smoke test) lift this deliverable from *solid* to *strong*; without them, just tag cleanly as hypothesis. (Not feasible in the time window? Clean tagging is enough — we don't expect market research.)
4. **Marketing mini-brief:** one ICP, one channel, 3 hypothetical ads (headline + body + visual idea), a landing-page hero (headline, subhead, CTA, 3 value bullets), and one success metric per asset ("success = …").

### Optional stretch (this is how you stand out)

Build a **working mini-automation** (n8n, Make, Zapier, or a Custom-GPT) that handled part of *your own* work — e.g. market/competitive research (CSRD consultants, ESG tools), generating ad variants, or analysing survey data. Explain the system briefly. This demonstrates "automate yourself" concretely.

> **On the 20 % "AI-Leverage" dimension:** How you use and verify AI in your work process (visible in your decision log + prompts) already counts in full. The optional automation is the path to the *top* of this dimension, not the entry ticket.

### Business scoring

| Dimension | Weight |
|---|---|
| Commercial reasoning (bottom-up, Unit Economics, consistent assumptions) | 25% |
| Customer insight / ICP (sharp segment, assumptions tagged) | 20% |
| AI leverage / "automate yourself" | 20% |
| Prioritisation / scrappiness (what you cut & why) | 15% |
| Marketing / positioning (ICP fit, channel fit, success triggers) | 10% |
| Communication / storytelling | 10% |

---

## Ground rules, submission & timeline

**Effort:** approximately 4–6 focused hours. You have a 7-calendar-day window from receipt — that window is for *flexibility*, not for grinding. Please don't over-invest: we assess thinking and judgment, not polish. *(The 4–6 hours include the walkthrough and decision log. Loom: 1 take, 3–5 min; decision log: 5–10 bullet lines.)*

**Use any AI, any library, search freely.** This is expected, not just allowed. Cursor, Claude, Copilot, coding agents — go for it.

**A rough core with clear thinking beats a polished but shallow result.** More hours do not mean more points; we assess the core outcome, not time invested.

**Equal opportunity:** AI Factory Austria is committed to equal opportunity. Whether you come from university, a bootcamp, or are self-taught — what counts is *how* you think and work with AI. If you need support or adjustments in the process, let us know.

### What to submit

1. **Repo link** (GitHub/GitLab) with code + README *(Dev track)* or documents *(Business track)*.
2. **Walkthrough (1 take, 3–5 min, max 5):** a Loom or screen recording. Show your result and explain *how* you built/researched it — especially the AI steps. *(No video possible or preferred? A concise written walkthrough counts equally — just let us know.)*
3. **Short decision log + key AI prompts:** 5–10 lines of decisions/trade-offs plus the AI prompts that made a difference. Show us *how you work with AI* — that is exactly the skill we are hiring for.
4. **Self-report:** how many hours did you invest? (Honest answer — no penalty points.)

**Submission:** by email to aiandbusinessgrowth@ai-at.eu. Your specific deadline and any upload link are in the accompanying email.

**Response time:** we get back to you within ~10 working days with a slot for the live debrief or a brief update.

**The live debrief (30–45 min):** you walk us through your result, we set *one new requirement live* and watch how you extend your own work. The new requirement is deliberately small — it's about thinking out loud, not producing a perfect result in 10 minutes. You may use your usual AI tools, exactly as when building. Afterwards we show you our own solution and talk honestly about it.

**Fair & transparent:** this challenge is unpaid. In return, after the debrief we show you our own reference solution — with real decisions, prompts, and trade-offs. That is our "learn" promise in action. And: structured, honest feedback for everyone, whatever the outcome. No ghosting. Ever.

---

## Data & privacy

The seed dataset is synthetic/simplified (as of 2026-06) and does not represent an official AI:AT position. No domain knowledge is required — the ESG KPIs are self-explanatory. Field documentation is in [`./data/README.md`](./data/README.md) (kept in German for now).

Your submitted documents (repo link, Loom link, files, prompts) will be used solely for the hiring decision, will not be shared with uninvolved third parties, and will be deleted no later than **six months** after the conclusion of the selection process (or earlier on your request), in accordance with GDPR. The legal basis is the initiation of a possible employment relationship (Art. 6 GDPR); you may request access or deletion at any time. Questions: aiandbusinessgrowth@ai-at.eu.

---

🇦🇹 *If anything is unclear, the German original in this repo is authoritative.*

> **Traduzione della community** — Questa è una traduzione italiana del brief della challenge in tedesco, affinché i candidati internazionali possano leggerla e cimentarsi. I file in tedesco di questo repository (`README.md`, `dev/`, `business/`) sono la fonte autorevole. Domande? Scrivi a aiandbusinessgrowth@ai-at.eu. Fatto per divertimento e per imparare 🌍

---

## Lo scenario

I team di Regulatory Affairs e Legal nei settori regolamentati (energia, finanza, farmaceutica, telecomunicazioni) perdono tempo ogni giorno a sfogliare manualmente siti web parlamentari e liste RIS, alla ricerca di progetti di legge e mozioni che riguardano la propria azienda. Chi reagisce in ritardo perde le scadenze per i pareri o viene colto di sorpresa da nuovi obblighi di conformità.

**Parlamentsmonitor** prende un elenco di procedimenti parlamentari e un profilo aziendale, riassume l'impatto di ciascun procedimento sull'azienda, assegna un punteggio di impatto e restituisce il risultato come digest prioritizzato — il briefing di allerta precoce che ogni mattina attende sulla scrivania.

---

## Scegli il tuo percorso

| Ruolo | Di cosa si tratta | Inizia qui |
|---|---|---|
| **Sviluppatore/trice IA** | Costruisci l'agente Parlamentsmonitor + una breve code review | 📂 [`dev/`](./dev/) |
| **Analista Business IA & Venture Builder** | È un business? Business Case + Go-to-Market | 📂 [`business/`](./business/) |

> Sai già dalla nostra conversazione quale percorso è il tuo — vai semplicemente nella cartella giusta. In caso di dubbi, mandaci una breve email. (Curiosi dall'altra parte? Dai pure un'occhiata. Solo la tua cartella conta per la tua consegna.)

---

## 🛠️ Percorso Sviluppatore/trice IA

Benvenuto/a. Non è un test trabocchetto. È un piccolo, autentico pezzo del lavoro che svolgiamo ogni giorno nel Venture Studio e nell'n8n CoE: costruire qualcosa di utile rapidamente con l'IA.

Non esiste una soluzione modello da raggiungere. Valutiamo come scomponi un problema poco specificato, prendi decisioni e usi l'IA in modo significativo.

### La missione

I team di Regulatory Affairs e Legal nei settori regolamentati (energia, finanza, farmaceutica, telecomunicazioni) perdono tempo ogni giorno a sfogliare manualmente liste RIS e siti web parlamentari, alla ricerca di progetti di legge e mozioni che riguardano la propria azienda. Chi reagisce in ritardo perde le scadenze per i pareri o viene colto di sorpresa da nuovi obblighi di conformità.

Costruisci un «Parlamentsmonitor»: un piccolo agente IA che prende un elenco di procedimenti parlamentari e un profilo aziendale, riassume l'impatto di ciascun procedimento sull'azienda (LLM-summarise), assegna un punteggio di impatto e restituisce il risultato come digest prioritizzato — il briefing di allerta precoce che ogni mattina attende sulla scrivania.

Forniamo un seed dataset con 21 procedimenti parlamentari sintetici (`../data/vorgaenge.json`, campi documentati) e un profilo aziendale di esempio (`../data/examples/profil_energie.json`). Non è necessaria alcuna conoscenza del dominio: tutto ciò di cui hai bisogno si trova nel dataset e in questo brief.

> 📂 **Nel repository:** [`../data/`](../data/): `vorgaenge.json` + profilo di esempio (doc dei campi: [`../data/README.md`](../data/README.md)).
> Schema «Event-Poll → LLM-Summarise → Impact-Score → Digest»: caricare i procedimenti, filtrarli e valutarli, riassumere, produrre un report prioritizzato.

### Parte A: Costruire l'agente (obbligatoria)

- **Input:** un profilo aziendale (`branche`, `themen_interessen`, `impact_schwelle`) più un elenco di procedimenti (dal seed; un percorso live opzionale verso la vera API parlamentare, vedi sotto).
- **Output:** un digest prioritizzato con i procedimenti più importanti al di sopra della `impact_schwelle`, ordinati per punteggio di impatto, ciascuno con titolo, tipo, stato, data, un breve riassunto dell'impatto sull'azienda (una frase) e una raccomandazione (es. «Alta priorità: procedimento in corso, settore principale» o «Monitorare: rilevante a medio termine»).
- **Seam obbligatorio:** il passaggio LLM-summarise (che genera un breve riassunto per ciascun procedimento) deve essere intercambiabile. Uno stub deterministico offline funziona senza chiave né connessione di rete; un vero provider LLM è un percorso opzionale (env/flag). L'esecuzione predefinita non richiede chiave API.
- **Forma:** un repository Git eseguibile con codice reale e un README che ci permette di avviare il sistema in meno di 5 minuti (offline, senza passaggi di build, Node ≥ 20). La scelta dello stack è tua (una CLI TypeScript è la scelta più naturale).

> **Le decisioni progettuali interessanti:** Come calcoli il punteggio di impatto? Il tipo di procedimento (proposta governativa vs. mozione), lo stato (in corso vs. concluso), la corrispondenza settoriale e la sovrapposizione dei temi sono tutti fattori rilevanti; come li pesi dipende da te. Allo stesso modo: come separi in modo pulito il seam LLM (stub e provider reale) senza complicare eccessivamente il resto della pipeline? E: cosa entra nel digest, cosa viene scartato? Ci interessa il ragionamento, non una formula prestabilita. È esattamente qui che vediamo il tuo giudizio.

> Una vera chiamata LLM è consentita ma non obbligatoria. Uno stub deterministico (es. derivato dal campo `kurztext` del seed, o un semplice template) è perfettamente accettabile per la consegna obbligatoria se non hai una chiave API. Stretch opzionale: connessione reale a un LLM di tua scelta e percorso live verso l'API OGD parlamentare (anche senza chiave).

### Parte B: Code review (~15 min)

Ti forniamo un breve snippet di codice generato da IA (TypeScript; non è richiesta esperienza con TypeScript — il bug è comprensibile indipendentemente dal linguaggio). Suggerimento: confronta ciò che il commento di documentazione *promette* con ciò che il codice *fa*, e segui mentalmente l'esecuzione con un piccolo esempio. C'è un bug funzionale centrale. Trovalo, correggilo e giustifica in 3–5 frasi perché è un bug. Dicci anche cosa noti per il resto — casi limite, assunzioni discutibili, modellazione dei tipi, test mancanti. Quella critica più ampia conta quanto la correzione stessa. Vogliamo vedere se sei in grado di *valutare* l'output dell'IA, non solo di generarlo.

> Lo snippet si trova in [`./dev/code-review/snippet.ts`](./dev/code-review/snippet.ts).

### Punteggio percorso Sviluppatore/trice

| Dimensione | Peso |
|---|---|
| Funzionalità (funziona, soddisfa il nucleo) | 20% |
| Scomposizione e giudizio (ambiguità risolta con criterio, buoni trade-off) | 20% |
| Collaborazione con IA / processo (come hai sfruttato e verificato l'IA) | 20% |
| Qualità del codice e gusto (leggibile, manutenibile, «slop» IA individuato) | 15% |
| Comunicazione / documentazione (README, decision log, walkthrough) | 15% |
| Test (test significativi, niente teatro della copertura) | 10% |

> La Parte B (code review) non è inclusa nella tabella sopra. È un segnale separato con un valore informativo particolarmente elevato sul tuo giudizio riguardo al codice generato da IA, e può fare la differenza in decisioni equilibrate.

---

## 📊 Percorso Analista Business IA & Venture Builder

Benvenuto/a. Questo è un lavoro autentico di Venture Studio: valutare la maturità commerciale di un'idea e renderla vendibile — in una settimana, con l'IA come leva.

### Lo scenario

Il nostro team tecnico sta sviluppando un prototipo: «Parlamentsmonitor», un agente IA che interroga l'API Open Data del Parlamento austriaco per rilevare nuovi progetti di legge e mozioni, riassume l'impatto per le aziende di ciascun procedimento, assegna un punteggio di impatto e restituisce il risultato come digest prioritizzato. Pubblico di riferimento: team di Regulatory Affairs e Legal nei settori regolamentati (energia, finanza, farmaceutica, telecomunicazioni) che ogni giorno sfogliano manualmente le liste parlamentari e in questo modo perdono scadenze per i pareri o vengono sorpresi da nuovi obblighi di conformità. Il tuo compito: è un business valido? E come lo portiamo sul mercato?

Forniamo come orientamento un seed dataset con 21 procedimenti parlamentari sintetici (`../data/vorgaenge.json`) e un profilo aziendale di esempio. Lo stesso dataset è condiviso con il percorso Dev. *I procedimenti illustrano il problema (complessità regolatoria, lavoro di monitoraggio manuale); i tuoi clienti paganti sono le aziende nei settori regolamentati che hanno bisogno di regulatory intelligence.*

> ⚠️ **Importante per il sizing:** I dati non contengono deliberatamente cifre di mercato, prezzi o conversione (mostrano solo procedimenti parlamentari sintetici e profili di esempio). Tu ricerchi/stimi autonomamente il numero di clienti raggiungibili (es. quanti team di Regulatory Affairs esistono nei fornitori di energia austriaci o negli istituti finanziari), il prezzo del prodotto e il tasso di conversione; l'IA e il web sono lì esattamente per questo (fonti benvenute). I profili di esempio servono ad affinare il tuo ICP/segmento, non a derivare cifre di volume.

Per questa analisi, tratta Parlamentsmonitor come un venture commerciale autonomo, separato dal contesto AI:AT (non commerciale, finanziato dall'UE).

### Deliverable (limitati: valutiamo il pensiero, non il design delle slide)

**1. Lean Canvas** per «Parlamentsmonitor» (con focus sul problema).

**2. Business Case di una pagina** con:
- **Dimensione del mercato bottom-up.** La forma conta: `‹team di clienti raggiungibili› × ‹prezzo mensile› × ‹conversione›`. *Per favore, niente «1 % di un mercato enorme» — un numero derivato vale più di uno grande senza derivazione.* Rendi visibile il ragionamento dietro ogni fattore. Il prezzo stesso fa parte della tua analisi: giustificalo invece di darlo per scontato (collegarlo al valore che lo strumento porta a un team di Regulatory Affairs è un buon approccio). *(Esempio di forma da un altro settore, solo per illustrare la struttura: 800 aziende artigiane regionali × €29/mese × 5 %.)*
- **Unit Economics approssimative** (CAC, ARPU/LTV, Payback). *In breve: quanto costa un/a cliente (CAC) rispetto a ciò che porta (ARPU per mese, LTV nel corso della vita), e dopo quanti mesi il CAC è recuperato (Payback)? Stime approssimative ma giustificate sono sufficienti.*
- **L'assunzione più rischiosa identificata + un test economico per validarla.**

**3. ICP + Value Proposition** per un segmento (es. solo la conformità dei fornitori di energia, o solo gli istituti finanziari con un dipartimento normativo). Etichetta ogni assunzione come *validata* o *ipotesi*. Anche 2–3 segnali rapidi (brevi conversazioni con le persone target o uno smoke test di landing page) elevano questo deliverable da *solido* a *forte*; senza di essi, etichetta semplicemente in modo chiaro come ipotesi. (Non fattibile nel lasso di tempo? Un'etichettatura pulita è sufficiente — non ci aspettiamo una ricerca di mercato.)

**4. Mini-brief di marketing:** un ICP, un canale, 3 annunci ipotetici (headline + body + idea visiva) + un hero di landing page (headline, sottotitolo, CTA, 3 bullet di valore) + una metrica di successo per asset («successo = …»).

**Stretch opzionale (così ti distingui):** Costruisci una mini-automazione funzionale (n8n, Make, Zapier o un Custom-GPT) che ha gestito parte del *tuo stesso* lavoro — es. ricerca di mercato/competitiva su strumenti di Regulatory Intelligence, generazione di varianti di annunci, analisi di fonti di settore. Spiega brevemente il sistema. Questo dimostra concretamente il principio «automatizza te stesso/a».

> **Sulla dimensione «IA-Leverage» al 20 %:** Come usi e verifichi l'IA nel tuo processo di lavoro (visibile nel decision log + prompt) conta già pienamente. L'automazione opzionale è il percorso verso la *vetta* di questa dimensione, non il biglietto d'ingresso.

### Punteggio percorso Business

| Dimensione | Peso |
|---|---|
| Ragionamento commerciale (bottom-up, Unit Economics, assunzioni coerenti) | 25% |
| Conoscenza del cliente / ICP (segmento preciso, assunzioni etichettate) | 20% |
| IA-Leverage / «automatizza te stesso/a» | 20% |
| Priorizzazione / scrappiness (cosa hai tagliato e perché) | 15% |
| Marketing / posizionamento (adeguatezza ICP, adeguatezza canale, trigger di misura) | 10% |
| Comunicazione / storytelling | 10% |

---

## Regole del gioco, consegna e calendario

**Impegno:** circa 4–6 ore concentrate. Hai una finestra di 7 giorni di calendario dalla ricezione — quella finestra è per la *flessibilità*, non per sgobbare. Non sovrainvestire: valutiamo il pensiero e il giudizio, non la rifinitura. *(Le 4–6 ore includono il walkthrough e il decision log. Loom: 1 ripresa, 3–5 min; decision log: 5–10 righe di appunti.)*

**Usa qualsiasi IA, qualsiasi libreria, cerca liberamente.** Ci si aspetta questo, non è solo consentito. Cursor, Claude, Copilot, agenti di codice — vai.

**Un nucleo grezzo con pensiero chiaro batte un risultato rifinito ma superficiale.** Più ore non significano più punti; valutiamo il risultato di fondo, non il tempo investito.

**Pari opportunità:** AI Factory Austria è impegnata nelle pari opportunità. Che tu provenga dall'università, da un bootcamp o sia autodidatta — ciò che conta è *come* pensi e lavori con l'IA. Se hai bisogno di supporto o adattamenti nel processo, faccelo sapere.

### Cosa consegnare

1. **Link al repository** (GitHub/GitLab) con codice + README *(percorso Dev)* o documenti *(percorso Business)*.
2. **Walkthrough (1 ripresa, 3–5 min, max 5):** un Loom o una registrazione dello schermo. Mostra il tuo risultato e spiega *come* hai costruito/ricercato — specialmente i passaggi IA. *(Niente video possibile o preferito? Un walkthrough scritto sintetico vale uguale — comunicacelo.)*
3. **Breve decision log + prompt IA chiave:** 5–10 righe di decisioni/trade-off e i prompt IA che hanno fatto la differenza. Mostraci *come lavori con l'IA* — è esattamente la competenza per cui stiamo assumendo.
4. **Autovalutazione:** quante ore hai investito? (Risposta onesta — nessuna penalità.)

**Consegna:** tramite email a aiandbusinessgrowth@ai-at.eu. La scadenza precisa e il link di upload, se previsto, si trovano nell'email di accompagnamento.

**Tempi di risposta:** ti ricontatteremo entro ~10 giorni lavorativi con uno slot per il debrief live o un breve aggiornamento.

**Il debrief live (30–45 min):** ci presenti il tuo risultato, aggiungiamo *un nuovo requisito in diretta* e osserviamo come estendi il tuo stesso lavoro. Il nuovo requisito è deliberatamente piccolo — si tratta di pensare ad alta voce, non di produrre un risultato perfetto in 10 minuti. Puoi usare i tuoi soliti strumenti IA, esattamente come durante la costruzione. Poi ti mostriamo la nostra soluzione e ne parliamo onestamente.

**Equo e trasparente:** questa challenge è non retribuita. In cambio, dopo il debrief ti mostriamo la nostra soluzione di riferimento — con decisioni reali, prompt reali e trade-off reali. Questa è la nostra promessa di «apprendimento» in azione. E: feedback strutturato e onesto per tutti/e, qualunque sia il risultato. Nessun ghosting. Mai.

---

## Dati e privacy

Il seed dataset è sintetico/semplificato (a partire da 2026-06) e non rappresenta una posizione ufficiale di AI:AT. I procedimenti parlamentari sono modellati sulla semantica reale dell'API Open Data del Parlamento austriaco, ma sono interamente fittizi — nessun procedimento legislativo reale, numero o contenuto. Non è richiesta alcuna conoscenza del dominio; i campi sono autoesplicativi e documentati in [`./data/README.md`](./data/README.md) (mantenuto in tedesco per ora). *(Percorso Business: le cifre di mercato/prezzi per il sizing non sono nei dati — le ricerchi tu stesso/a, vedi il tuo brief.)*

I tuoi documenti inviati (link al repository, link Loom, file, prompt) saranno utilizzati esclusivamente per la decisione di assunzione, non saranno condivisi con terze parti non coinvolte e saranno eliminati al più tardi **sei mesi** dopo la conclusione del processo di selezione (o prima su tua richiesta), in conformità con il GDPR. La base giuridica è l'avvio di un possibile rapporto di lavoro (Art. 6 GDPR); puoi richiedere accesso o cancellazione in qualsiasi momento. Domande: aiandbusinessgrowth@ai-at.eu.

---

🇦🇹 *In caso di dubbio, il testo originale in tedesco in questo repository è quello autorevole.*
